pamphlet_excerpts: A properly working plumbing system protects: Plumbing systems carry water into and out of a home through a system of pipes (p. 20).

A properly working plumbing system protects Principle 2: For the health and safety of the people who live there, the water entering the home through the water-supply system must be pure and clean (p. 20).
A properly working plumbing system protects Principle 3: Wastewater should never come into contact with the water that the family uses for drinking, bathing, or washing clothes and dishes (p. 20).

step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (A properly working plumbing system protects): Plumbing regulations have been developed to help make sure that plumbing is installed and maintained correctly (p. 20).
Step 2 (A properly working plumbing system protects): These regulations, commonly called plumbing codes, are important in preventing the water-supply system from becoming contaminated (p. 20).
Step 3 (A properly working plumbing system protects): National plumbing codes exist that give specific regulations for all plumbing operations (p. 20).
Step 4 (A properly working plumbing system protects): Many communities have adopted these regulations or amended them to fit their local needs (p. 20).

quiz_item.question: What is the primary purpose of the curved P-trap installed directly beneath every household sink, shower, and floor drain?
options: A. To boost incoming municipal water pressure before it reaches the hot and cold faucet valves.
B. To grind up solid food waste so it does not enter the septic tank or city sewer main.
C. To hold a standing water seal that blocks toxic, flammable, and foul-smelling sewer gases from rising out of the drain-waste-vent system into the building.
D. To filter dissolved calcium and magnesium minerals out of potable drinking water.
choices: A. To boost incoming municipal water pressure before it reaches the hot and cold faucet valves.
B. To grind up solid food waste so it does not enter the septic tank or city sewer main.
C. To hold a standing water seal that blocks toxic, flammable, and foul-smelling sewer gases from rising out of the drain-waste-vent system into the building.
D. To filter dissolved calcium and magnesium minerals out of potable drinking water.
quiz_item.correct_answer: C. To hold a standing water seal that blocks toxic, flammable, and foul-smelling sewer gases from rising out of the drain-waste-vent system into the building.

pamphlet_excerpts: Careers & Professional Pathways: Plumbing, including pipe fitting, is an important and well-paid occupation (p. 8).
Careers & Professional Pathways Principle 2: It covers installations and repairs in homes, commercial properties, and factories (p. 8).
Careers & Professional Pathways Principle 3: Plumbing pipelines are used for water supply, waste drainage, natural-gas heating, and many other purposes (p. 8).
Careers & Professional Pathways Principle 4: As a Scout, your major interest in plumbing probably will be in the field of home repairs (p. 8).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Careers & Professional Pathways): If a faucet leaks, a pipe freezes, or a plumbing fixture does not operate properly, you will want to know how to evaluate the problem (p. 8).
Step 2 (Careers & Professional Pathways): Then you will be able to decide on the proper steps to take to fix the problem, or determine that the job requires a professional plumber (p. 8).
Step 3 (Careers & Professional Pathways): When you discover a plumbing problem, you can often take care of basic plumbing needs, but remember that a plumber is like a doctor (p. 8).
Step 4 (Careers & Professional Pathways): For serious trouble or problems beyond your ability, you should get help from a trained specialist (p. 8).

B. To grind up solid food waste so it does not enter the septic tank or city sewer main.
